lines.say: 96.6% recall on LongMemEval, with zero API calls and no LLM at all.
This is MemPalace, a free and open-source memory system for AI that runs local first.
It stores your conversation history as verbatim text, and finds it again with semantic search.
Nothing leaves your machine unless you opt in. ChromaDB is the default backend, and it needs no configuration.
The hybrid mode reaches 98.4% on 450 held-out questions that were not seen during tuning.
Add an LLM rerank on top, and recall climbs to 99% or more.
The team still refuses to headline 100%, because the last 0.6% came from inspecting specific wrong answers.
It also ships 45 MCP tools, a temporal knowledge graph, and its own wing and diary for every agent.
One warning from the README: Claude Code sessions expire in 30 days without auto-save hooks wired.
To start, run uv tool install mempalace, then mempalace init on your project. You need Python 3.9 or newer and about 300 MB of disk.
Send this to someone whose agent forgets everything between sessions.
MemPalace. Your AI's memory, kept on your machine.
